[A790] TAKEN
Branch: `925-srp-ta-tf` at `16ba667d` (#901's review head)
Authoritative references: #925; #665 issuecomment-6904803181 (finding 18) and issuecomment-6904832963; IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.4 (a talker declares one Talker attribute for a stream, Advertise or Failed), 35.2.6 (a Talker registration of the other type replaces the one held), 35.2.2.8, 35.2.2.7.2; Milan v1.2 4.2.7.2.2; `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/README.md` (the Listener rules, and the processor comparison's "conflicting New registrations retain Failed precedence").
Interpreted scope: lwSRP withdraws a registered Talker of the other type only on a received JoinIn/JoinMt and leaves a conflicting New to the host's precedence rule. The split adapter's rule is Failed first (`srp_mbx.c` `interested_msrp` and the registrar walk), so a Talker Advertise's New over a still-registered Talker Failed keeps the Listener at Asking Failed until the talker's next MRPDU. The fix is in the adapter, not lwSRP: per bound sink, the most recently registered of the two kinds decides the Listener declaration and the kind ACMP sees, the other kind deciding once the latest leaves. The release's processor does the same (every registering event sets the sink's registered type). No SRP timer or bound changes, and nothing changes in the mailbox contract or RTL.
Validation plan: GoogleTest units at 1x1/1if and 8x8/2if for TF->TA and TA->TF in both orders (separate MRPDUs and one MRPDU), leave of either, coincident registrations and binding replacement, each rule with a planted defect caught by name in the SRP mutant campaign; the firmware self-test, fw_coverage --check (new code 100 % of branches), the SRP/firmware campaigns, the verilator-suites shards with the split firmware, elaborate, docs; the CPU service-budget harness at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if (every row within its bound, stated costs from measurement); both split platform images (1x1/1if, 8x8/1if) with timing, ROM and area reported; the release image checked byte-identical by hash. All on a clean clone of the final head.
Blockers: none

[A790] STOP: both split images miss the +0.030 ns floor on all three directives, by 6 to 22 ps; the base's 1x1/1if image misses it too

**What stopped.** I ran S9's recipe for the image built at `a9f0dbc0`: the builder's split placement, the export, the
integrated route and its signoff corners, then the other two directives from that route's synthesis checkpoint, one
Vivado at a time. On no directive are WNS and WHS >= +0.030 ns at every corner. Every route closed with 0 failing
endpoints and 0 routing errors; only the margin floor is missed.

| 1x1/1if | Slow WNS / WHS | Fast WNS / WHS | Short of the floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| ExtraPostPlacementOpt (recipe) | +0.024 / +0.092 | +1.660 / +0.036 | setup, 6 ps |
| ExtraTimingOpt | +0.008 / +0.050 | +1.641 / +0.023 | setup 22 ps, hold 7 ps |
| AltSpreadLogic_high | +0.177 / +0.050 | +1.641 / +0.023 | hold, 7 ps |

| 8x8/1if | Slow WNS / WHS | Fast WNS / WHS | Short of the floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| ExtraPostPlacementOpt (recipe) | +0.011 / +0.070 | +1.370 / +0.034 | setup, 19 ps |
| ExtraTimingOpt | +0.171 / +0.102 | +1.636 / +0.014 | hold, 16 ps |
| AltSpreadLogic_high | +0.215 / +0.102 | +1.636 / +0.014 | hold, 16 ps |

**The base misses too.** I routed the base's own 1x1/1if image (`16ba667d`, #901's review head, without this change)
through the same recipe. Its AltSpreadLogic_high run is queued for CPUs; its result goes to the lane's handoff.

| 1x1/1if at `16ba667d` | Slow WNS / WHS | Fast WNS / WHS | Short of the floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| ExtraPostPlacementOpt (recipe) | +0.208 / +0.051 | +1.636 / +0.014 | hold, 16 ps |
| ExtraTimingOpt | +0.260 / +0.053 | +1.636 / +0.014 | hold, 16 ps |

**Where the margin goes.** None of the worst paths is reached by this change:
- Setup: the mailbox register read path (`KL_mbx/rd_off_r` to `reg_rdata_r`, S9's known path) at 1x1, and the
  datapath's audio-map edit path (`KL_mbx_cdc/u_edit/rq_r` to `amap_edit_oclaim_expect_r`) at 8x8.
- Hold: the TDM render FIFO's clock-crossing BRAM write port (`chan_tdm_render/u_fcdc/mem_r`) at 1x1, the FIFO
  the base misses on too, and the AAF clock meter (`aaf_clock_meter/s2_ts_r` to `grp_ts0_r`) at 8x8.

The change is firmware only. The exported gateware equals the base's at both shapes, apart from LiteX's comment tree:
the same netlist, the same route script. Only the ROM's contents differ: 88 B more firmware at 1x1, so `rom_bank3`
holds 722 words where it held 700, in the same bank; 32 B more at 8x8, in its one bank. Vivado optimises through ROM
contents, so a different image places differently.

**Everything else is green.** Heads: `a9f0dbc0` (the image), and `1be0a6c4` (a test file's line wrap and
`srp_mbx.c`'s coverage counts, no image input).
- Firmware self-test: suites PASS; control 716 of 716, AECP 299, SRP 441 caught (the 10 new plants at both interface
  counts), 0 escaped. The SRP shard again at `1be0a6c4`: 441 caught, 0 escaped.
- `fw_coverage --check` PASS: `srp_mbx.c` at 741/741 lines and 671/671 branches after its standing exclusions.
- Workflow replays, step by step on fresh clones: every job of rtl-fast, elaborate and docs failed 0. The three
  mutant jobs ran as their campaign commands above. `docs` and `firmware-unit` ran again at `1be0a6c4`, which wraps
  the 121-column line the Python idiom gate found at `a9f0dbc0`.
- `plat_ledger.py` PASS at every point, with the 8x8/2if `ctrl_plat` record raised to 20,416 B (same 60.5 RAMB36).
  ROM is +88 B at 1x1 and +32 B at 8x8; 8x8/1if still plans 56.0.
- The release image is byte-identical: `bios.bin` and the stripped ELF at both configs.
- Split boots PASS at 1x1 and 8x8.
- Service budget at 1x1/1if, rc 0: 96 groups, 0 refusals, 0 of 129,813 passes over the share. The flip check at
  1x1/1if passes with every row within its bound; the load gate passes (0.517 / 0.514).
- Service budget at 8x8/1if: 95 groups, 0 refusals, 0 of 266,195 passes over the share. It exits 1 on STATED lines
  for the polls' base, ACMP's item and ACMP's declined offer over the one-interface statements, which that point
  holds to 1x1/1if's: the shape's known excess, the same classes as #894's 8x8/1if gate (#894 issuecomment-6867393730, item (b)). None of these is SRP's.
- Both points record the same 7 probe misses, all in `backlog-owed` (ACMP and AECP records behind seven owed frames).
  #919's branch records the same 7 on this harness at 1x1/1if.
- No stated cost changes: the SRP items measure within their statements at both points, and at 1x1/1if they measure
  2,733 cycles (walk) and 25,078 (an SRP record), rule figures 30 and 265 µs, statements 35 and 280.

**Decision needed.** The base's own image misses the floor too, by 16 ps on hold. Do you accept one of these routes for the
images (1x1/1if's AltSpreadLogic_high: WNS +0.177, WHS +0.023; 8x8/1if's: WNS +0.215, WHS +0.014)? Or should the
routes use directives or seeds outside S9's three, or something else? The fix itself is done: in `95426618`, the
latest registered of Talker Advertise and Talker Failed decides the Listener declaration (IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.4,
35.2.6), with its tests. Nothing is pushed.

[A10] Ruling on the STOP above: **the route misses are the base's, not this change's.** Your own base route of `16ba667d` misses at 1x1/1if on the same FIFO, and #919 and #920 measured the same 8x8/1if figures at `659d7687`. The gateware is identical apart from ROM contents. These misses are now #927 (scope widened in #927's comments), which is in the flip train ahead of this PR.

For this lane, both routes are recorded as "misses at the base, owed to #927", with the figures. It is not a stop and not a debt of this PR. No seeds or extra directives.

Round 2:
- one `--no-ff` merge of dev-soft-core `70f4056f`, with the affected rows re-measured;
- the verilator-suites sweep;
- then REVIEW READY.

The 8x8/1if stated-cost lines are #914's (per-shape statements), as at the base. Record them as such.

[A790] REVIEW READY
Commit: `09a948d4`, branch `925-srp-ta-tf`. It is three commits on `16ba667d` (#901's review head), then one `--no-ff` merge of dev-soft-core `70f4056f` (#901's merge). `70f4056f`'s tree is `16ba667d`'s, so the merge changes no file. Not pushed; the manager pushes and opens the PR.

Changed:
- `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/srp_mbx.c` / `.h`: of a stream's Talker Advertise and Talker Failed, the one registered latest decides each binding's Listener declaration and the kind ACMP sees while it stays registered; the other decides once it leaves (IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.4, 35.2.6).
  - lwSRP replaces the other type only for a JoinIn/JoinMt and registers a New beside it. The adapter now records the order from lwSRP's indications (`latest_kind`, `listener_kind`).
  - The receive filter and the registrar walk were Failed first, which held Asking Failed until the talker's next MRPDU. An Advertise New over a registered Failed is now Ready within a JoinTime.
  - A binding made later takes the StreamID's latest from any binding of it.
  - No SRP timer or bound changes; lwSRP, the mailbox contract and RTL are unchanged.
- Tests: `srp_mbx.cpp` `SrpTalkerKinds` (6) and `srp_feedback.hpp` (2). They cover both replacements, leave of either kind in both orders, coincident registrations in one MRPDU in both orders, a later binding, the fallback, and ACMP's view.
- Plants: `srp_kind_mutants.py` adds ten, one a rule, each caught by name at both interface counts. The `failed-listener-ready` plant moved to its new site.
- `srp/README.md` states the rule. The ledger records `ctrl_plat` at 8x8/2if as 20,416 B (+64), the same 60.5 RAMB36. `coverage.ratchet` holds `srp_mbx.c` as measured.

Validation (clean clones; `1be0a6c4` has the merge's tree, so its results are `09a948d4`'s):
- Firmware self-test (at `a9f0dbc0`): suites PASS; control 716 of 716, AECP 299, SRP 441 caught, 0 escaped. The SRP shard again at `1be0a6c4`: 441, 0 escaped.
- `fw_coverage --check` PASS: `srp_mbx.c` 741/741 lines, 671/671 branches after its standing exclusions.
- Workflow replays, step by step on fresh clones: in every job of rtl-fast, elaborate and docs, each step ran rc 0 or is a hosted-only step not run, with its reason stated. The three mutant jobs ran as their campaign commands above. `docs`, `firmware-unit` and `changes` ran again at `1be0a6c4`.
- `plat_ledger.py` PASS at every point. ROM is +88 B at 1x1 and +32 B at 8x8; 8x8/1if still plans 56.0. The release image is byte-identical: `bios.bin` and the stripped ELF at both configs.
- Service budget at 1x1/1if, rc 0: 96 groups, 0 refusals, 0 of 129,813 passes over the share.
- Rows, re-run on the merge's clone: the flip check at 1x1/1if passes with every row within its bound (`last` 136.65 of 140 ms, `txL` 48.58 of 49); the load gate passes (0.517 / 0.514 against 0.70). Over every point, the flip check exits 1 at 8x8/2if alone, which is reported and not held, as at the base.
- Service budget at 8x8/1if: 95 groups, 0 refusals, 0 of 266,195 passes over the share. Its STATED lines (the polls' base, ACMP's item, ACMP's declined offer) are #914's per-shape statements, as at the base. None is SRP's, and SRP's items are within at both points.
- Both points record the same 7 probe misses, all in `backlog-owed`, pre-existing. No stated cost changes.
- The merge affects no row. Every image the budget legs and routes used relinks byte-identical at `09a948d4` (budget 1x1 `311430e7`, 8x8/1if `6d2a5d0e`, routes `e85cd3a5`, `b648575d`), so round 1's legs at `a9f0dbc0` carry.
- Routes, both shapes: misses at the base, owed to #927, per issuecomment-6908876793. Figures are Slow WNS / Fast WHS in ns, image at `a9f0dbc0` = `09a948d4`'s:

| Shape | ExtraPostPlacementOpt | ExtraTimingOpt | AltSpreadLogic_high |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1x1/1if | +0.024 / +0.036 | +0.008 / +0.023 | +0.177 / +0.023 |
| 8x8/1if | +0.011 / +0.034 | +0.171 / +0.014 | +0.215 / +0.014 |
| 1x1/1if at the base `16ba667d` | +0.208 / +0.014 | +0.260 / +0.014 | not run |

- No seeds or extra directives were run, and no further route is owed: the merge changes no image.
- Verilator-suites sweep at `09a948d4`: 65 suites in 4 shards, every one with a recorded pass: shard 0 15 of 15, shard 2 17 of 17, shard 3 16 of 16, shard 1 14 of 17. Shard 1's other three, one contention failure (`gptp_shadow`'s fixed 12 s lifecycle timeout, its 325 checks passing) and two wall-clock cuts (`milan_dp_gm_steps`, `milan_dp_render`), each passed when re-run uncontended. The shards' tallies total 2,713,029 checks, 0 in-suite failures.

Acceptance criteria: the desk part is met (above). The bench part, Listener Ready within 1 s of the Talker Advertise, is the gating run's.

Open risks/questions:
- A binding that saw neither registration's indication keeps Failed first until the talker's next MRPDU leaves one kind. That needs every binding of the StreamID unbound and one bound again inside the conflict window; it is documented in the README.
- `srp_mbx.cpp` at the 8x8 entity, a shape no gate runs that suite at, fails two startup tests at `16ba667d` too.
- `coverage.ratchet` holds three AECP lines below their measurement at the base; they are not this change's.
- The shards ran one or two at a time (memory and CPU limits) and were completed across host restarts. Every cut run recorded no rc and is not cited. Shard 2 ran with the hosted job's 4-core budget (`VERILATOR_JOBS=4 SIM_JOBS=4`): without it, `capture_coherence` builds with every host core and overran the 10 GB unit cap.

[A10] **Ruling on a conflict between the specifications** (raised by R849-1 F1, PR #932 issuecomment-6930031527): Talker Advertise and Talker Failed both registered for one stream on one port.

- **IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.6** replaces a registered Talker of the other type only on a received JoinIn or JoinMt. Its NOTE, which is informative, says that if both are received, Talker Failed takes precedence.
- **Milan v1.2 5.3.8.5** is normative: "If a Talker Advertise attribute with matching SRP parameters is being received, the PAAD-AE shall be declaring an MSRP Listener Ready attribute".
- **IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.1.2.1** has a talker declare one of the two per stream and move directly between them. So a coexisting pair is a transition caught mid-way, and the newer registration is the talker's current state.

**Decision:** the split follows the normative Milan clause. The kind registered most recently decides the Listener declaration and what ACMP sees, as #665 finding 18 found the release processor's in-place swap does. The informative 802.1Q NOTE is a documented departure, recorded here and in `sw/firmware/ctrl/srp/README.md` with these clauses. Specifications are authoritative (owner, 2026-10-18), and the normative text wins over an informative note.

**When the latest kind leaves while the other is still registered,** the split falls back to the older kind. The release processor instead unregisters the sink on any leave. The README's comparison table records this difference. PR #932 keeps the fallback, because it follows the registrations that remain (R850-1 F2 keeps the order for their lifetime).

[A790] REVIEW READY
Commit: `5f625090`, branch `925-srp-ta-tf`, six commits after reviewed head `09a948d4` (PR #932). Round 3 combines the R850-1 and R849-1 responses under #925 issuecomment-6930043105. Nothing pushed.

Changed:

- R850-1 F1: the receive filter retains transmission work when its observation changes the desired Listener kind. Trailing unchanged or ignored messages no longer lose that work. Idle-timer tests inspect Listener declarations and ACMP GET_RX_STATE; atomic replacement, retained withdrawal ordering and final-state-only declarations are preserved.
- R850-1 F2: latest-kind order survives the final unbind, rebinding, and in-place identity replacement for the lifetime of the retained StreamID registrations. Either registration ending, expiry included, or the owning interface resetting releases the held entry. The bounded table follows the registration-pool capacity. The old fallback exception test and plant are replaced.
- R849-1: corrected clause record (802.1Q-2018 35.1.2.1; 35.2.6's JoinIn/JoinMt rule and informative Failed-precedence NOTE; Milan v1.2 5.3.8.5 and the manager ruling); README comparison records release unregister-on-either-leave versus split fallback. Added repeated New from a two-kind state and in-place rebind checks; exact reviewer plants `r849-renew-not-recorded` and `r849-bind-copy-skipped-for-self` are caught. Removed the source comment's report-local label.
- Seven new tests, three extended, one removed; 23 rule plants (21 at both interface counts, two at two interfaces). No SRP timer, approved budget bound, mailbox contract, submodule or RTL change.

Validation, on clean clones:

- `python3 sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_ctrl_firmware.py --require-rv32 --self-test --jobs 4 --shard N/4`, N=0..3: all rc 0; 79 suite arms; control 716/716, AECP 299 and SRP 465 plants caught, zero escaped.
- `python3 sw/firmware/gtest/fw_coverage.py --check --jobs 4`: rc 0, 39 files PASS; `srp_mbx.c` 768/768 lines and 695/695 counted branches, with its three standing exclusions unchanged.
- R850-1 `run_reproduce.py`, `run_probes.py`, `run_rebind.py`: rc 0 at one and two interfaces, including controls without a trailing message, 200 phase/direction cases and 216 ordered-event traces per count. The reproductions observe model delay 0 ms; the idle-timer tests pass within a JoinTime. These are model results, not physical timing acceptance.
- R849-1 probes pass: 22 tests at one interface and 23 at two. Its two named plants above are caught at both counts. The unchanged legacy mutant driver still selects the removed fallback test for `r849-unknown-withdraws` and calls that selection an escape; its identical production mutation is caught by replacement plant `feedback-latest-unknown-withdraws` against the unreachable full-table guard. This limitation is recorded explicitly.
- Docs and firmware-unit/changes workflow replays: executable steps rc 0; setup/hosted-only steps have recorded reasons for not running. Elaborate replay and its final verifier are rc 0: 10 executed steps, 36 not run with reasons, zero bad.
- `plat_ledger.py`, `test_ctrl_memory.py`, `flip_grade.py --check --point 1x1/1if`, and `load_grade.py --check`: rc 0. The statement rows and load are unchanged.
- `python3 -B tb/verilator/ctrl_service_budget/run.py --point <point> --build-dir <dir> --record-budget-findings --record-share-findings --jobs 7`, at `1x1` and `8x8-1if`: 96/95 groups, zero refusals and zero share overruns in 137530/247150 work passes. All SRP and THE TRANSMIT rows are within bounds; SRP record apply peaks 237.99/222.20 us against 280 us, and timer-driven MRPDU response peaks 1.87123/2.62353 ms against the measured row's 20 ms bound. No late, absent or unresolved timer work; join intervals 189.053–190.070 / 188.316–190.122 ms against 181–239 ms. Both shapes retain the same seven pre-existing backlog-owed misses, with no new missed path.

The 1x1 run is rc 0. The 8x8 run is rc 1 only for #914's per-shape statements under #925 issuecomment-6908876793: 81 polls-base, two ACMP-item and four declined-offer records, versus 77/3/4 in round 2. Their peaks changed from 244.99/66.56/25.22 us to 270.00/63.91/21.96 us; measurement + 5%, rounded upward to 5 us, gives 285/70/25 us, against the existing 225/55/20 us statements. These remain #914's statement work; no approved bound or source cost statement is changed here. Every measured cost delta and its rounded value is recorded in the packet's two budget summaries, including decreases and costs not directly staged by these groups.

- Release firmware rebuilt at `5f625090`: `bios.bin` and stripped ELF byte-identical to `16ba667d` at both shapes. CPU-budget ELFs measured at `7a2def7c` relink byte-identical at `5f625090`; the only intervening change is the coverage-count record.

Platform ROM by shape (1x1/1if, 1x1/2if, 8x8/1if, 8x8/2if): 118128, 119712, 130752, 132304 B, deltas +552/+552/+520/+520 from round 2. RAMB36 allocations are 43/44/56/61; only 8x8/2if grows, by half a tile. Its ledger entry is raised under the owner rule (#665 issuecomment-6892332745), as S14 debt.

Routes remain **misses at the base, owed to #927** (#925 issuecomment-6908876793). WNS/WHS minima in ns, for ExtraPostPlacementOpt / ExtraTimingOpt / AltSpreadLogic_high respectively: 1x1/1if +0.024/+0.036, +0.008/+0.023, +0.177/+0.023; 8x8/1if +0.011/+0.034, +0.171/+0.014, +0.215/+0.014. Gateware exports match round 2 apart from generated comments and ROM contents; no new route or routed LUT/FF area is claimed.

Acceptance: requested desk fixes and scoped verification are complete under the recorded #914/#927 dispositions. The physical Listener Ready within one second check remains the manager's gating run, and both reviewers must review the corrected head. The round 3 packet contains HANDOFF-r3.md, the full updated PR-BODY.md, this comment and a generated receipt index. The manager archives and publishes it; no new round 3 full sweep is claimed.
